langStringDefinitionTypeIec61360.text: A fixed classification of process types according to the nature of the action performed on material or product.
A process step in which a part or material is intentionally changed in its physical or chemical characteristics, or joined with another part.
A process step in which a product or material is examined and compared against a standard for quantity, quality, or characteristics, without being intentionally altered.
A process step in which a product or material is moved from one location to another.
A process step in which a product or material is kept under controlled conditions for a planned or unplanned interval, retrievable when needed.
A process step in which a product or material is held awaiting the next planned action, without work being performed on it.
A process step that restores a nonconforming product to a condition acceptable for its intended use, entered only by units identified as nonconforming.
A collection of criteria and reference material used to determined whether a product or process output conforms to a required standard.
The identification of the specific standard and smapling methodology applied to determine conformance during inspection.
An identifier referencing the specific document or code that defines an applicable standard.
The method by which units are selected for inspection from a lot or batch.
The quality level, expressed as percent defective, that is the worst tolerable process average when a continuing series of lots is submitted for sampling inspection.
The defined threshold values against which an inspection or process result is judged accptable or unacceptable.
The quality level, expressed as percent defective, that a sampling plan is desinged to reject with a stated high probability.
A collection of source documents supporting the definitions and criteria specified wihtin a quality specification.
A collection of individual instances of a process, each representing one manufacturing step defined by its inputs, outputs, duration, and the resource that performs it.
A unique identifier assinged to a single instance of a process within a production system.
A label indicating a logical or organizational grouping of related process instances, used for assignment or reporting purposes independent of process sequencing.
A scope identifier indicatin which product variant's process flow a process instance belongs to, or a shared value indicating the instance applies uniformly across all variants.
A collection of references to the immediate predecessor process instances that a process instance depends on for its readiness.
References to the immediate predecessor process instances that a process instance depends on for its readiness.
The duration required to complete one execution of a process instance, expressed in seconds.
The nominant electrical power consumption of a process instance while actively running, expressed in kilowatts.
The proportion of output from a process instance that fails to conform to its requires specification.
A collection defining the materials consumed and produced by a process instance, together with the duration required to carry it out.
A list of materials consumed as input by a process instance, each with its identity and quantity.
A list of materials produced as output by a process instance, each with its identity and quantity.
A reference to the identity of a specific material, part, or intermediate item involved in a process instance.
The amount of a referenced material consumed or produced, expressed in the unit defined for that material.
A collection of references to the resources responsible for carrying out a process instance.
A reference to the human resource responsible for performing a process instance.
A reference to the stationary tool or machine used to preform a process instance.
A reference to the automated, non-human resource responsible for perfoming a process instance without direct human operation.
A reference to the quality standard or criteria against which a process instance's output is evaluated for conformance.
A collection of scalar statistical characteristics describing how a process instance behave when it operates
